explanation: The Western 'OK' meaning of this gesture doesn't reliably carry over in Saudi Arabia: general references on obscene gestures note it carries vulgar or offensive connotations in parts of the Middle East, and some Gulf sources associate the gesture, especially when shaken toward someone, with invoking the evil eye. Evidence specific to Saudi Arabia is thin, so treat the gesture as genuinely unpredictable rather than clearly safe or clearly offensive.
local_tip: Use a thumbs-up-free verbal 'tamam' (fine) instead of the OK hand sign to avoid ambiguity.
